scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Internal traffic between Office A and Office B works fine.
DSWs/CSWs report all OSPF neighbors Full. But Internet-bound
traffic (e.g., reaching 203.0.113.1) from any internal PC
times out. R1 itself can reach internal devices but cannot
reach the ISP gateways. Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 default route
Mechanism: r1 is the only egress to the ISPs. Without a
  default route, packets destined to public IPs (anything
  not in 10.0.0.0/8 or 203.0.113.0/30) have no next hop on
  r1 and are dropped. Internal traffic stays inside the
  OSPF domain so it's unaffected. The fact that r1's
  OSPF neighbors are still Full distinguishes this from
  an OSPF daemon failure.
Localization: r1
Root cause: default route missing from r1's routing table
Fix: re-add default — `ip route add default via 203.0.113.1`
  (or restart frr if it was sourced via OSPF default-information
  originate from an ISP)
scenario.fix_spec:
re-add default — `ip route add default via 203.0.113.1`
  (or restart frr if it was sourced via OSPF default-information
  originate from an ISP)

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: OSPF default route origination on r1 (FRR daemon). Mechanism: Access switches and distribution/core switches have full OSPF adjacency and exchange internal routes, so inter-office traffic works. However, when hosts try to reach the Internet (e.g., 203.0.113.1), their first-hop DSW replies “Destination Net Unreachable” because it has no route to external networks and no OSPF-learned default. This is evidenced by PC pings failing with ICMP Net Unreachable sourced from 10.1.0.2 (dswa1 SVI) and by the absence of 0.0.0.0/0 in dswa1/csw1/csw2 routing tables. Localization: r1 FRR OSPF config has “default-information originate” but r1’s RIB has no default route, so OSPF doesn’t inject a default into the fabric. On r1, ip route shows no default; only connected 203.0.113.0/30 and 203.0.113.4/30. r1 itself can ping ISP peers (203.0.113.1 and .5) because those are directly connected, confirming the problem is not the ISP links but the lack of default propagation. Root cause: r1 is missing a default route in its RIB, so OSPF does not originate a default toward the LAN. Corrective fix: Install a default route on r1 to the ISP(s), e.g., “ip route add 0.0.0.0/0 via 203.0.113.1” and optionally a secondary via 203.0.113.5 with higher metric, or change FRR to “default-information originate always.” After adding the default, OSPF will advertise 0/0, DSWs/CSWs will install it, and Internet-bound traffic from PCs will forward to r1 and out to the ISPs.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly localizes the problem to r1 (mentions r1 FRR, r1's RIB lacking a default, and directs fixes for r1).
The agent explicitly identifies the missing default route on r1 (and its absence from the RIB/OSPF origination) as the root cause and corrective target.
The report explicitly notes full OSPF adjacencies and that FRR is running but not injecting a default, distinguishing the issue from an OSPF daemon failure.
Provides the expected remediation — add a default route on r1 (ip route 0.0.0.0/0 via 203.0.113.1) or configure FRR to always originate the default, which will restore OSPF‑advertised 0/0.

The logs clearly show PCs getting ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable' from 10.1.0.2 (dswa1) while r1 can reach the ISP peers, which supports the inference that the LAN edge lacks an external route. However, the investigation did not include an explicit capture of r1's routing table showing the missing 0.0.0.0/0 (nor an explicit ospf neighbor table), so the key claim that r1's RIB lacks the default is plausible but not directly shown in the visible outputs.
